Gamma function

Gamma function is a definite integral whose integrand depends on one variable.
It is also known as Euler’s integral of second kind.
It is the generalization of factorial notation from integer values to real numbers.

Transcript block 1 (source interval 000000-000299 seconds):
[00:00:00.548] Hello everyone, I am Kavishri, Assistant Professor in the Department of Science and Humanities. I welcome all of you to special functions, which is your fifth unit in engineering mathematics one.
[00:00:14.820] In this unit, you are going to learn gamma function, beta function, and basis function. In this particular class, we are going to discuss definition of gamma function.
[00:00:29.092] Properties of gamma function and graph of gamma function. Gamma function is a definite integral whose integrant depends on one variable. It is also known as Euler's integral of second kind.
[00:00:46.436] It is the generalization of factorial notation from integes to real numbers. We can define gamma function as
[00:00:56.868] Gamma of n is equal to integral zero to infinity t power minus x power n minus one dx n greater than c. Thus gamma n defines a function of n for positive values of n.
[00:01:17.636] From this result we can obtain the value of gamma. So let us put n is equal to 1 in the definition of gamma function. Then we get gamma 1 is equal to integral 0 to infinity e power minus x x power 1 minus 1 dx.
[00:01:38.020] x power 1 minus 1 is x power 0 and we know x power 0 is 1, so it just reduces to integral 0 to infinity e power minus x bx.
[00:01:51.268] And we know that integration of e power minus x dx is equal to e power minus x divided by minus 1.
[00:02:00.868] Using the fact that e power minus infinity is equal to 0 and e power 0 is equal to 1, we can evaluate this to 1. Thus we have gamma of 1 is equal to 1.
[00:02:18.436] We can have an alternate form of gamma function. We can obtain it easily by using definition of gamma function. We know that gamma n is equal to integral 0 to infinity t power minus x x power n minus 1 dx.
[00:02:37.092] In this expression, let us substitute x is equal to t square. If x is t square, dx is 2t d.
[00:02:47.908] Therefore, gamma n is equal to integral 0 to infinity e power minus t square t square to the power n minus 1 2 t dt.
[00:03:01.860] Observe here, after this substitution, the limits of integration do not change because when x is equal to 0, your t is also 0. When x is infinity, t is also infinite.
[00:03:20.004] So it reduces to 2 times integral 0 to infinity t power minus d square t to the power 2n minus 1 dt. This is another form of gamma function.
[00:03:34.564] While solving problems on gamma function, we can make use of any of these two forms according to our convenience. Next, we will discuss some properties of gamma function. First of them is reduction formula.
[00:03:52.580] It states that gamma of n plus 1 is equal to n gamma n where n is a real number. We can prove this easily by using the definition of gamma function, which is
[00:04:07.236] Gamma n is equal to integral 0 to infinity e power minus x x power n minus 1 dx.
[00:04:15.812] We want gamma of n plus 1. So let us just replace n by n plus 1 in this expression. So we get gamma of n plus 1 is equal to integral 0 to infinity e power minus x x power n plus 1 minus 1 dx.
[00:04:36.004] which is equal to integral 0 to infinity e power minus x x power n dx. We have to evaluate this integral by using integration by parts. We know already that integration by parts
[00:04:53.668] is given by integral uv dx is equal to u into integral v dx minus integral of derivative of u or d by dx of u into integral of v dx.

Transcript block 2 (source interval 000300-000599 seconds):
[00:05:10.532] When you take x power n is equal to u and e power minus x is equal to v, you will get it as x power n e power minus x divided by minus 1 plus n into integral 0 to infinity.
[00:05:27.472] E power minus x power n minus one dx. When you substitute the limits of integration for the first term,
[00:05:37.700] E power minus infinity zero and e power zero is one. So first term becomes a zero and observe the second term along with n, you have integral zero to infinity, e power minus x, x power n minus one.
[00:05:54.304] dx which is nothing but equal to gamma n. So your gamma of n plus 1 is n into gamma n. So this is the reduction formula which is very very important result.
[00:06:10.852] When n is a negative non-integer, the formula used to find gamma of n is gamma n is equal to gamma of n plus 1 divided by n. Remember, gamma n is not defined for n is equal to 0.
[00:06:29.060] And it is also not defined when n is a negative integer. But we can find the value of gamma n if n is negative real number which is not a negative integer using this formula.
[00:06:47.972] When n is a positive integer, gamma of n plus one is equal to n factory. We can prove this easily by using reduction formula which states gamma of n plus 1 is equal to n gamma n.
[00:07:03.428] Let us put n is equal to 1 in this formula, we get gamma 2 is equal to 1, gamma 1. That is 1, because we know gamma 1 is equal to 1.
[00:07:15.300] When we put n is equal to 2, we get gamma of 3, that is 2 gamma 2, which is 2 factorial. When you put n is equal to 3, we get gamma 4, which is 3 gamma 3, that is 3 factorial.
[00:07:32.740] And when you put n is equal to 4, we get gamma 5, which is 4 gamma 4, that is 4 factor.
[00:07:42.148] Just look at the pattern here. Gamma two is one factorial, gamma three is two factorial, gamma four is three factorial, and gamma five is four factorial. So we can write in general
[00:07:57.168] Gamma of n plus 1 is equal to n factorial where n is a positive integer. Remember, gamma n is not defined when n is 0 or when n is a negative integer.
[00:08:16.100] Gamma half value we can find now. So this is also very very important result. Gamma half is equal to square root of pi.
[00:08:25.732] We can prove this by considering alternate form of gamma function, which is gamma n is equal to 2 times integral 0 to infinity e power minus x square x to the power 2n minus 1 dx.
[00:08:42.148] Let us put n is equal to half in this expression. So you get gamma half, which is equal to 2 times integral 0 to infinity, a power minus x square dx.
[00:08:55.940] Which can also be written as two times integral 0 to infinity e power minus y square dy.
[00:09:04.420] Because since we are dealing with definite integrals, here x is a dummy variable. You can write it as x or y or t or any variable since we are dealing with definite integrals.
[00:09:18.980] So gamma half whole square is gamma half into gamma half we can consider this as two times integral zero to infinity e power minus x square dx into two times integral zero to infinity e power minus y square dy.
[00:09:36.644] which is equal to four times integral 0 to infinity 0 to infinity e power minus x square plus y square dx d y.
[00:09:48.356] Now let us make use of polar coordinates by putting x is equal to r cos theta, y is equal to r sin theta. Then x square plus y square is equal to r square.

Transcript block 3 (source interval 000600-000899 seconds):
[00:10:03.556] And dx dy is equal to r dr d theta. And observe the limits for x and y. Both are varying from 0 to infinity. That means both x and y are positive.
[00:10:23.364] So our region of integration is the first quadrant. In this first quadrant, r value varies from 0 to infinity and theta value varies from 0 to pi by 2.
[00:10:38.980] So we can write gamma half the whole square is equal to 4 times integral 0 to pi by 2, 0 to infinity, e to the power minus r square r dr d theta.
[00:10:55.076] Then it can be written as four into integral 0 to pi by 2 b theta into integral 0 to infinity e power minus r square r br
[00:11:09.060] When you integrate the first integral 0 to pi by 2 d theta, integration of d theta is theta, substitute the limits of integration, it reduces to 4 into pi by 2.
[00:11:23.524] into integral 0 to infinity e power minus r square r dr. That is equal to 2 by into minus 1 by 2 e power minus r square limits vary from 0 to infinity.
[00:11:42.180] So here the evaluation of integral is done by taking the substitution r square is equal to t, hence 2 r dr is equal to dt.
[00:11:54.404] Thus, we get gamma half the whole square is equal to pi, so we can conclude gamma half is equal to square root of pi, which is a very very important result. Now let us find the graph of the gamma function.
[00:12:11.972] Before that, just have a glance at this table where gamma n values are given for various values of n between 1 and 2. This is the graph of gamma function.
[00:12:24.260] Observe here, gamma function is continuous for positive values of n and it is not continuous for negative values of n. We can find or you can plot this curve by using the properties gamma of n plus 1 is equal to n gamma n.
[00:12:41.028] Gamma n is equal to gamma n plus 1 divided by n. This is for negative real numbers which are not indigenous. And gamma half is equal to square root of pi. And also referring to the table which is given in the previous slide. Just try
[00:12:59.012] With these properties and the table, try to get the shape. This is very interesting thing. You can really do it. You will enjoy doing it. With this, we will end the session. Thank you.
